title: Detects "variable[key]" as a left- or right-hand assignment operand.
Elevation of privilege: Unauthenticated access to notes endpoints
description:
An anonymous visitor calls notes endpoints without a session. If any route lacks the authentication middleware, they can read or write notes.

Framework stride, element 'Anonymous request', likelihood medium, impact high, rated high.
remediation: - Apply authentication middleware to all notes routes by default and return 401 with no data when no valid session exists. (ASVS V8.2.1, V8.1.1, V4.1.1)

title: Tampering: Forged owner_id or cross-site request plants or changes notes
description:
An attacker sends a create or update request with a forged owner_id field, or tricks a signed-in user's browser into a cross-origin POST/PUT/DELETE without a CSRF token, planting or altering notes under the victim's account.

Framework stride, element 'Notes request', likelihood high, impact high, rated critical.
remediation:
- Take owner id only from the server-side session and ignore any client-supplied owner fields. (ASVS V8.2.2, V2.2.1)
- Require a CSRF token or SameSite cookies plus Origin checking on all state-changing notes requests. (ASVS V3.5.1, V3.3.2)
- Validate note text as a non-empty string within a maximum length and reject unexpected fields. (ASVS V2.2.1, V2.1.1)

title: Data disclosure: Note text cached by browsers or proxies and visible to later users of the device
description:
Responses carrying private note text could be stored in the browser cache, back/forward cache or a shared proxy. On a shared device, another person could then read a previous user's notes after sign-out.

Framework linddun, element 'Notes response', likelihood medium, impact medium, rated medium.
remediation: - Send Cache-Control: no-store on all authenticated notes responses. (ASVS V14.3.2, V14.2.5)

title: Non compliance: Deleted notes and deleted accounts leave note data behind with no retention limit
description:
The plan does not say what happens to notes when a user deletes a note or their account. Soft deletes, backups or orphaned rows could keep personal content indefinitely. This breaks erasure and storage-limitation duties such as GDPR Art. 17 and Art. 5(1)(e).

Framework linddun, element 'Notes DB', likelihood medium, impact medium, rated medium.
remediation: - Hard-delete notes when the user deletes them, and cascade-delete all notes when the account is deleted. Define a retention period for backups and purge expired data. (ASVS V14.2.7, V14.1.2)

title: Repudiation: Denied access and note changes are not logged or attributable
description:
Cross-user access attempts, auth failures and writes may go unlogged, so an attacker can deny the action and the owner cannot detect probing. Logging note text would itself leak private content.

Framework stride, element 'Web app', likelihood medium, impact medium, rated medium.
remediation:
- Log security events with user id, note id, action, outcome and timestamp, and exclude note text. (ASVS V16.3.1, V16.3.2, V16.2.1, V14.2.4)
- Protect logs from tampering and injection by encoding or sanitizing logged values. (ASVS V16.4.1, V16.4.2)

title: Information disclosure: Note text or errors leak data in responses
description:
Verbose errors, stack traces or cacheable responses can expose private note text or internals to the user, shared caches or the browser history.

Framework stride, element 'Notes response', likelihood medium, impact medium, rated medium.
remediation:
- Send Cache-Control no-store on notes responses and return generic error messages without stack traces. (ASVS V14.3.2, V16.5.1)
- Return only the required note fields. (ASVS V15.3.1)

title: Information disclosure: Notes DB contents exposed at rest or in transit
description:
Private note text is stored in the database. Without protection of database credentials, file access and the connection, an attacker with host or network access can read all notes. The flow is listed with HTTPS but is internal.

Framework stride, element 'Read note result', likelihood low, impact high, rated medium.
remediation:
- Restrict database file and credential access to the app account and protect secrets outside source code. (ASVS V13.3.1, V14.1.2)
- Encrypt the database connection if it is remote, and consider encryption at rest for sensitive note text. (ASVS V12.3.1, V14.1.1)

title: Denial of service: Oversized or high-volume note requests exhaust the service
description:
An authenticated or anonymous client sends very large note bodies or floods create and list requests, exhausting memory, CPU or database storage.

Framework stride, element 'Web app', likelihood medium, impact medium, rated medium.
remediation:
- Limit request body size and note length, and apply rate limiting plus a per-user note quota. (ASVS V2.1.1, V2.4.1, V15.2.2)
- Paginate the list endpoint. (ASVS V15.2.2)

title: Data disclosure: Private note text stored in plaintext and exposed through DB access or backups
description:
Notes are sensitive free text and may hold health, financial or relationship details. They are stored unencrypted in Notes DB. Anyone with DB, snapshot or backup access can read every user's notes, including operators who have no need to see them. The plan leaves encryption at rest as an open question.

Framework linddun, element 'Notes DB', likelihood medium, impact high, rated high.
remediation: - Encrypt the note text column or the database volume at rest. Keep keys outside the database and restrict DB and backup access to least privilege. (ASVS V14.1.2, V14.2.1, V11.3.1)

title: Data disclosure: Note text leaks into logs, error messages or telemetry
description:
Request bodies, validation errors or DB errors may be written to application logs or returned in error responses. Log readers who should not see private notes would then have access to them, and the logs would outlive the notes themselves.

Framework linddun, element 'Web app', likelihood medium, impact medium, rated medium.
remediation: - Log only user id, note id and outcome. Never log note text or request bodies, and return generic error messages to clients. (ASVS V16.2.5, V16.5.1, V14.2.4)

title: Tampering: SQL injection through note text or id
description:
Note text or note id containing SQL metacharacters is concatenated into a query, letting an attacker read, change or delete other users' notes.

Framework stride, element 'Store note query', likelihood medium, impact high, rated high.
remediation: - Use parameterized statements for all queries and validate the id type. (ASVS V1.2.4, V2.2.1)

title: Tampering: Stored script in note text executes in the browser (XSS)
description:
An attacker saves a note with HTML or script content. If the app renders it as HTML without encoding, it runs in the owner's session and can steal data or perform actions.

Framework stride, element 'Web app', likelihood medium, impact high, rated high.
remediation:
- Return notes as JSON or plain text, or output-encode contextually when rendering HTML. (ASVS V1.2.1, V1.1.2)
- Set X-Content-Type-Options nosniff and a restrictive Content-Security-Policy. (ASVS V3.4.4, V3.4.3)

title: Elevation of privilege: Missing ownership check on edit and delete lets users modify others' notes
description:
A user sends PUT or DELETE with a victim's note id, or includes an owner_id field to reassign a note. Without an ownership check on every write, they gain write access to notes they do not own.

Framework stride, element 'Web app', likelihood high, impact high, rated critical.
remediation: - Enforce ownership in the data-access layer on every update and delete, with the owner id in the query condition, and never allow owner reassignment. (ASVS V8.2.2, V8.3.1, V8.2.1)

title: Unawareness: Users are not told how their notes are stored, kept or deleted, and cannot export them
description:
Users enter sensitive content, but the design includes no privacy notice. It does not say whether notes are encrypted, how long they are kept, or what happens on account deletion, and it gives no way to export or erase all of their notes. Users cannot make informed choices or exercise their data rights.

Framework linddun, element 'Signed-in user', likelihood medium, impact medium, rated medium.
remediation: - Document the personal data stored, its purpose, retention and deletion behaviour, and show this to users. Provide a way to export and delete all of their own notes. (ASVS V14.1.1, V14.2.7)

title: Information disclosure: Insecure direct object reference exposes other users' notes
description:
An attacker changes the note id in GET requests or enumerates ids to read another user's private notes. The list endpoint could also return notes unfiltered by owner.

Framework stride, element 'Notes request', likelihood high, impact high, rated critical.
remediation:
- Filter every read and list query by the session owner id and return 404 for notes the caller does not own. (ASVS V8.2.2, V8.3.1, V4.2.1)
- Do not rely on id secrecy; use unguessable ids as defence in depth. (ASVS V8.2.2)

title: Information disclosure: Unauthorized responses reveal whether a note or account exists
description:
Differing status codes or messages for missing versus forbidden resources let an attacker enumerate valid note ids or users.

Framework stride, element 'Unauthorized response', likelihood low, impact low, rated low.
remediation: - Return identical generic 401 or 404 responses without revealing existence or details. (ASVS V16.5.1, V8.2.2)

title: Spoofing: Session hijack or forgery lets attacker act as a note owner
description:
Session identifiers travel with each notes request. If cookies lack Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite flags, or session ids are predictable or never rotated, an attacker can steal or forge a session and read or change another user's private notes.

Framework stride, element 'Notes request', likelihood medium, impact high, rated high.
remediation:
- Use high-entropy random session ids and set Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite cookie attributes; expire sessions on logout and idle timeout. (ASVS V7.2.1, V7.2.3, V3.3.1, V7.4.1)
- Serve all notes endpoints over TLS only and send HSTS. (ASVS V12.2.1, V3.4.1)

title: Data disclosure: Note text sent to the database over an unprotected connection
description:
The app-to-DB flow has no stated transport protection. If the database is remote or on a shared network, note text can be read in transit by anyone on that path.

Framework linddun, element 'Store note query', likelihood low, impact high, rated medium.
remediation: - Require TLS with certificate verification for the database connection, or restrict the DB to a local socket or private network. (ASVS V12.3.1, V12.3.3)
